# A defer f()? in a loop runs through pooled records, and the same program
# built with -d=nodefertrypool=1 runs through heap closures. Both builds
# print identical output [T-104.2]. The symbol check shows that the flag
# changes the lowering, so the comparison is not vacuous.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cp $GOROOT/test/logos/run/defer_try_semantics.lgo sem/main.lgo
cp $GOROOT/test/logos/run/defer_try_stress.lgo stress/main.lgo

cd sem
logos build -o $WORK/sem-pool$GOEXE .
go tool nm $WORK/sem-pool$GOEXE
stdout 'runtime\.deferprocTry'
exec $WORK/sem-pool$GOEXE
cp stdout $WORK/sem-pool.txt
logos build -gcflags=-d=nodefertrypool=1 -o $WORK/sem-heap$GOEXE .
go tool nm $WORK/sem-heap$GOEXE
! stdout 'runtime\.deferprocTry'
exec $WORK/sem-heap$GOEXE
cmp stdout $WORK/sem-pool.txt
cd ..

cd stress
logos build -o $WORK/stress-pool$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/stress-pool$GOEXE
cp stdout $WORK/stress-pool.txt
logos build -gcflags=-d=nodefertrypool=1 -o $WORK/stress-heap$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/stress-heap$GOEXE
cmp stdout $WORK/stress-pool.txt
cd ..

-- go.mod --
module example.com/pooldiff

go 1.27

-- sem/placeholder.txt --
-- stress/placeholder.txt --
